title: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
abstract: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract. In this study, the authors show that seasonal live-attenuated influenza vaccination provides cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus in ferrets, potentially through respiratory cellular immune responses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 鉴于美国奶牛中 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 的 暴发 及其感染包括人类在内的其他哺乳动物的能力,该研究旨在评估季节性流感 疫苗 对人源性牛 H5N1 流感病毒的保护作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了两种季节性流感 疫苗 对接受牛源 H5N1 分离株 A/Texas/37/2024 攻击的未接触过流感的雌性雪貂的保护功效。该研究于 2026 年进行,涉及以雪貂为 宿主 模型的受控实验设置。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用灭活流感 疫苗 和活减毒流感 疫苗 对雪貂进行免疫,然后用牛源性 H5N1 病毒攻击它们。他们测量了呼吸道和肺外组织中的病毒滴度并评估了疾病进展。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有未接种疫苗的雪貂都出现了严重的疾病并死于感染或被人道安乐死。疫苗接种 与灭活的 疫苗 降低了病毒滴度并延缓了疾病进展,但不能防止致命的结果。用减毒活 疫苗 免疫的六只雪貂中有五只在挑战中幸存下来,并显示出对鼻粘膜病毒复制的更有效控制。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,减毒活体 疫苗接种 会诱导更强的 T 细胞反应,这可能有助于抵御牛源性 H5N1 病毒,大多数免疫雪貂的存活和病毒复制减少就证明了这一点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,季节性减毒活流感 疫苗 可能针对抗原不同的 H5N1 病毒提供交叉保护,这可以为 疫苗 开发策略和针对人畜共患流感威胁的公共卫生准备提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于动物模型,不包括人类数据,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。证据是强有力的,因为它直接比较了 疫苗 在受控环境中的疗效和明确的结果。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 鉴于美国奶牛中 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 的 暴发 及其感染包括人类在内的其他哺乳动物的能力,该研究旨在评估季节性流感 疫苗 对人源性牛 H5N1 流感病毒的保护作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了两种季节性流感 疫苗 对接受牛源 H5N1 分离株 A/Texas/37/2024 攻击的未接触过流感的雌性雪貂的保护功效。该研究于 2026 年进行,涉及以雪貂为 宿主 模型的受控实验设置。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用灭活流感 疫苗 和活减毒流感 疫苗 对雪貂进行免疫,然后用牛源性 H5N1 病毒攻击它们。他们测量了呼吸道和肺外组织中的病毒滴度并评估了疾病进展。
analysis_zh.main_results: 所有未接种疫苗的雪貂都出现了严重的疾病并死于感染或被人道安乐死。疫苗接种 与灭活的 疫苗 降低了病毒滴度并延缓了疾病进展,但不能防止致命的结果。用减毒活 疫苗 免疫的六只雪貂中有五只在挑战中幸存下来,并显示出对鼻粘膜病毒复制的更有效控制。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,减毒活体 疫苗接种 会诱导更强的 T 细胞反应,这可能有助于抵御牛源性 H5N1 病毒,大多数免疫雪貂的存活和病毒复制减少就证明了这一点。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,季节性减毒活流感 疫苗 可能针对抗原不同的 H5N1 病毒提供交叉保护,这可以为 疫苗 开发策略和针对人畜共患流感威胁的公共卫生准备提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于动物模型,不包括人类数据,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。证据是强有力的,因为它直接比较了 疫苗 在受控环境中的疗效和明确的结果。

media_mentions.content_title: Nature Comms: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
media_mentions.content: Avian Flu Diary Covering Pandemic and Seasonal Flu, Emerging Infectious Diseases, public health, community & Individual preparedness. NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Thursday, November 26, 2026 Nature Comms: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus (translated) Credit University of Tokyo Press Release #19,430 Given the enormous logistics of creating, testing, manufacturing, and deploying a pandemic strain-specific vaccine (see Maggie Fox's SCI AM - A Bird Flu Vaccine Might Come Too Late to Save Us from H5N1), many researchers have looked for potential stop-gap benefits from seasonal flu vaccination. It's not a new idea (see 2008's Seasonal Flu Vaccine May Offer Some Protection To H5N1 and 2010's Seasonal influenza vaccine elicits heterosubtypic immunity against H5N1 that can be further boosted by H5N1 vaccination), but more recent studies have provided mixed and modest results at best. Some of those studies include: Nature Comms: Adjuvanted Influenza Vaccination Increases Pre-existing H5N1 Cross-reactive Antibodies mBio: Low levels of influenza H5N1 HA and NA antibodies in the human population are boosted by seasonal H1N1 infection but not by H3N2 infection or influenza vaccination EID Journal: Effect of Seasonal Influenza Vaccines on Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Ferrets EID Journal: Investigation of Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Neutralization by Quadrivalent Seasonal Vaccines, United Kingdom, 2021–2024 Our most recent foray into this topic was last September's EM&I: Limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccination before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferrets challenged with A(H5N1), which offered little encouragement on the effectiveness of using seasonal flu vaccines as a `prime-boost' for H5N1 vaccines. That said, there are known, or suspected, benefits to having been recently vaccinated against seasonal flu in the face of a pandemic strain. It still may provide some small boost to your immune response. HA neutralizing antibodies aren't the only immune defense against infection. The N1 component from H1N1 may provide some degree of protection against severe illness, although unlikely to prevent infection It could help prevent a co-infection with H5N1 and seasonal flu, which has the potential for being more severe. Co-infections could also help generate a reassorted `hybrid' virus (see Preprint: Intelligent Prediction & Biological Validation of the High Reassortment Potential of Avian H5N1 and Human H3N2 Influenza Viruses). Today, we've a study out of the University of Tokyo led by Yoshihiro Kawaoka and Professor Ryuta Uraki, that introduces a new wrinkle. Instead of only testing the standard quadrivalent flu shot (inactivated influenza vaccine), it adds a trivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV; FluMist) to the mix. Flumist is currently only available for those aged 2-49 in the United States, and carries a number of exclusions, including pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, or those who have recently received antiviral medications. As the graphic at the top of this blog indicates, those lab animals who received the live-attenuated influenza vaccine fared far better (83% survival vs 0%) than those which were inoculated with the standard flu shot. From the press release: When the immune responses involved in these protective effects were examined, no neutralizing antibodies against bovine-derived H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus were detected with any of the vaccines. On the other hand, the nasal attenuated live vaccine induced a stronger T-cell response to the virus than the inactivated vaccine. These results suggest that the nasal attenuated live vaccine also shows protective effects against bovine-derived H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus, and that this effect may be related to an immune response involving T cells. However, these results are based on animal experiments using ferrets and do not directly indicate infection prevention or severity prevention effects in humans. While an intriguing finding, there are a lot of caveats to consider, including: This was a small study using one H5N1 strain and a limited number of flu-naive ferrets. While useful in flu research, ferrets are not a perfect analog for humans, which invariably have a lengthy and messy history of exposures to influenza A viruses and/or vaccines. LAIV vaccines can only be safely used on a subset of society LAIV vaccines contain live-attenuated seasonal flu viruses, which could provide opportunities for a co-infection with a pandemic strain, with a theoretical potential for reassortment. The primary takeaway is not that LAIVs are a panacea for a pandemic, rather that nasal vaccines and T-cell immunity may be a promising direction for future pandemic flu protection. Of course, additional research might pave the way for LAIVs limited use in a future pandemic crisis. That said, it is a fascinating study, which many will want to read in its entirety. Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus Published: 25 November 2026 Volume 17, article number 11796 (2026) Ryuta Uraki, Kiyoko Iwatsuki-Horimoto, Maki Kiso, Mutsumi Ito, Seiya Yamayoshi, Masaki Imai & Yoshihiro Kawaoka Abstract Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract. (SNIP) Overall, seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination provided substantial protection against lethal hu-TX37-H5N1 infection in influenza-naive ferrets, whereas the inactivated vaccine reduced viral replication and delayed disease progression but did not prevent mortality. These findings suggest that immune responses beyond serum antibodies, including cellular and potentially mucosal immunity, may contribute to cross-protection against antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 viruses. title: Neuraminidase-based cross-protective immunity against H5N1 influenza viruses in humans
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus continues to expand globally across wild birds, poultry, and mammalian hosts, and the detection of genetic features associated with mammalian adaptation underscores the need to define pre-existing human immunity relevant to pandemic preparedness. Although serologic and vaccine studies have historically emphasized hemagglutinin (HA); neuraminidase (NA) is a key antigen capable of providing protective immunity. Here, we performed a retrospective analysis of NA-specific antibodies in human sera collected across 10 influenza seasons spanning the pre- and post-2009 pandemic periods. A total of 749 paired serum samples (1,498 total) were obtained prior to seasonal inactivated influenza vaccination (T1) and 28 days after vaccination (T2). NA-inhibiting antibodies were measured by enzyme-linked lectin assay using N1 antigens representing three genotypes (B.3.13, D1.1, and EA-2021-AB) from clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) viruses. HA responses were assessed by hemagglutination inhibition (HAI), and neutralizing antibodies by luciferase-based microneutralization. NA-inhibiting antibodies were detectable against all three genotypes across seasons, with measurable cross-reactive activity present in a substantial proportion of individuals before vaccination. Vaccination modestly increased NA-inhibiting titers, particularly after 2009–2010 following the introduction of A(H1N1)pdm09 into vaccine formulations. The highest responses occurred during post-pandemic seasons, suggesting enhanced cross-reactivity against H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses. In contrast, HAI activity against H5 was generally low or undetectable, despite detectable HA-reactive antibodies by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. These data indicate that cross-reactive NA-specific antibodies are present in human sera and can be boosted by seasonal vaccination, supporting increased consideration of NA in influenza serosurveillance and vaccine evaluation. IMPORTANCE The continued spread of A(H5N1) viruses and reports of mammalian adaptation markers heighten concerns about potential zoonotic transmission into humans. Most studies of human antibody responses focus on influenza HA, but NA is also an important immune target. By analyzing paired sera from humans collected over 10 influenza seasons, we show that NA-inhibiting antibodies cross-reacting with multiple contemporary genotypes from clade 2.3.4.4b A(H5N1) viruses are detectable and can be modestly but consistently boosted by seasonal inactivated influenza vaccination, particularly after the 2009 pandemic. The increase in cross-reactive NA responses observed during post-pandemic seasons suggests that A(H1N1)pdm09 exposure may have enhanced immunity recognizing contemporary H5N1 viruses. These findings highlight the importance of inducing NA-specific antibodies during influenza vaccination and of including NA in surveillance and in the assessment of vaccines intended to improve preparedness for emerging influenza viruses.

title: Molecular determinants of surface glycoprotein compatibility may explain the emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza A viruses
abstract: Abstract The emergence and spread of avian influenza viruses across diverse host species, exemplified by highly pathogenic clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses, depend in part on the functional compatibility between the surface glycoproteins hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA). However, the molecular determinants governing preferential HA-NA pairing remain unclear. Here, we show that clade 2.3.4.4b H5 HA with six glycosylation sites preferentially pairs with the full-length (long-stalk) N1 NA in birds and mammals. By contrast, H5 HA proteins from earlier clades with seven glycosylation sites preferentially pair with N1 NA proteins characterized by a stalk deletion (short-stalk). Our results indicate that the HA S/T160A mutation, observed in avian influenza viruses, abolishes the N158 glycosylation site and favors pairing with long-stalk N1, improving molecular compatibility and enhancing viral fitness. The N158 glycan underlies the preferential pairing of Gs/GD-lineage H5 viruses with short-stalk N1 proteins. These findings suggest that HA-NA pairing in avian influenza viruses is not an entirely stochastic process but is constrained by HA glycosylation status and NA stalk length, with implications for viral fitness and the emergence of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 viruses.

title: One Health priorities beyond 2026: translating advances in science, surveillance and governance into prevention and preparedness.
abstract: The interdependence of human, animal and environmental health and persistent gaps between multisectoral commitments and effective implementation were highlighted in The Lancet 2023 One Health series. Since then, advances in genomic and environmental surveillance, artificial intelligence and international governance have created new opportunities for infectious disease prevention and preparedness. However, avian influenza A(H5N1), filovirus outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance and the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak illustrate continuing challenges in surveillance, coordination and response. Climate-sensitive infections, foodborne zoonoses and environmental contamination further emphasize the need for integrated approaches extending beyond emerging viral threats. This review critically examines developments since 2023, distinguishing established preventive interventions from promising but incompletely validated technologies, and both proximate biosecurity controls and structural socio-ecological upstream prevention, from early detection and outbreak containment. We propose a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway linking detection, verification, joint risk assessment, accountable decisions, coordinated interventions and double-loop evaluation. An operational matrix illustrates its application across emerging and endemic infections, antimicrobial resistance and environmental threats. Five priorities address interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. Effective One Health implementation requires clear institutional responsibilities, sustained financing, co-designed community and indigenous participation and rigorous evaluation. Progress should ultimately be measured by demonstrable reductions in infectious disease risks and improved protection of human, animal and environmental health.

However, avian influenza A(H5N1), filovirus outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance and the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak illustrate continuing challenges in surveillance, coordination and response. Climate-sensitive infections, foodborne zoonoses and environmental contamination further emphasize the need for integrated approaches extending beyond emerging viral threats. This review critically examines developments since 2023, distinguishing established preventive interventions from promising but incompletely validated technologies, and both proximate biosecurity controls and structural socio-ecological upstream prevention, from early detection and outbreak containment. We propose a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway linking detection, verification, joint risk assessment, accountable decisions, coordinated interventions and double-loop evaluation. An operational matrix illustrates its application across emerging and endemic infections, antimicrobial resistance and environmental threats. Five priorities address interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. Effective One Health implementation requires clear institutional responsibilities, sustained financing, co-designed community and indigenous participation and rigorous evaluation. Progress should ultimately be measured by demonstrable reductions in infectious disease risks and improved protection of human, animal and environmental health.

abstract_zh: 《柳叶刀 2023 年同一个健康》系列强调了人类、动物和环境健康的相互依存性以及多部门承诺与有效实施之间持续存在的差距。从那时起,基因组和环境监测、人工智能和国际治理的进步为传染病预防和准备创造了新的机遇。然而,禽流感 A(H5N1)、丝状病毒 暴发、抗菌素耐药性和 2026 年安第斯病毒游轮 暴发 说明了 监测、协调和响应方面持续存在的挑战。气候敏感感染、食源性人畜共患病和环境污染进一步强调需要采取超越新出现的病毒威胁的综合方法。这篇综述批判性地审视了 2023 年以来的进展,将已建立的预防性干预措施与有前途但未完全验证的技术区分开来,并将近期生物安全控制和结构性社会生态上游预防与早期检测和 Z​​XQTERMXQXZ 遏制区分开来。我们提出了一个六阶段的 监测 行动路径,将检测、验证、联合风险评估、负责任的决策、协调干预和双环评估联系起来。操作矩阵说明了其在新发和地方性感染、抗菌素耐药性和环境威胁方面的应用。五个优先事项涉及可互操作的参与性 监测、基于证据的上游预防、综合抗菌素耐药性行动、纠正部门权力不对称的可持续国家治理以及公平的区域能力。有效的“同一个健康”实施需要明确的机构责任、持续的融资、共同设计的社区和土著参与以及严格的评估。最终应通过传染病风险的明显降低以及对人类、动物和环境健康的保护的改善来衡量进展。

title: Serologic Evidence of Avian Influenza Virus Exposure in Livestock, Egypt, 2024-2026.
abstract: Spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States sparked global concern. We investigated whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. We detected influenza H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%-4.5% of tested animals. Additional surveillance will elucidate host infection dynamics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether endemic avian influenza viruses are potentially spilling over into domestic livestock in Egypt. The research was motivated by global concern over the spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Egypt between 2024 and 2026, focusing on domestic livestock. It involved testing a sample of animals for evidence of avian influenza virus exposure.
analysis.methods: The researchers used serologic testing to detect antibodies against specific avian influenza subtypes in livestock. They analyzed the results to determine the prevalence of exposure to these viruses.
analysis.main_results: Influenza H9N2 antibodies were detected in 2.5% of tested animals, while H5N1 antibodies were found in 2.9%-4.5% of the sample.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be circulating in livestock, highlighting the need for further investigation into the dynamics of host infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the importance of additional surveillance to better understand the spread and impact of avian influenza viruses in livestock populations, which could inform public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides limited evidence due to its observational nature and the absence of detailed statistical analysis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential spillover of endemic avian influenza viruses into domestic livestock in Egypt between 2024 and 2026. Serologic testing revealed H9N2 antibodies in 2.5% of animals and H5N1 antibodies in 2.9%-4.5% of the sample. These findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be circulating in livestock, emphasizing the need for further surveillance to understand host infection dynamics. The study's observational design and lack of detailed statistical analysis limit the confidence in its conclusions, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

The research was motivated by global concern over the spillover of influenza A(H5N1) virus to cattle in the United States.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Egypt between 2024 and 2026, focusing on domestic livestock. It involved testing a sample of animals for evidence of avian influenza virus exposure.
elements_en.methods: The researchers used serologic testing to detect antibodies against specific avian influenza subtypes in livestock. They analyzed the results to determine the prevalence of exposure to these viruses.
elements_en.main_results: Influenza H9N2 antibodies were detected in 2.5% of tested animals, while H5N1 antibodies were found in 2.9%-4.5% of the sample.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that avian influenza viruses may be circulating in livestock, highlighting the need for further investigation into the dynamics of host infection.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the importance of additional surveillance to better understand the spread and impact of avian influenza viruses in livestock populations, which could inform public health strategies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides limited evidence due to its observational nature and the absence of detailed statistical analysis, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: In ovo administration of HA1-expressing Lactococcus lactis protects chicks against H9N2 infection via enhancing intestinal development and immune function
abstract: In this study, we utilized recombinant Lactococcus lactis (L. lactis) expressing the H9N2 AIV hemagglutinin (HA) subunit 1 (HA1) protein and evaluated its efficacy through in ovo vaccination. At embryonic day 17.5, 160 viable embryonated eggs were randomly assigned to four groups and inoculated with either PBS, an inactivated H9N2 vaccine, an empty L. lactis vector, or recombinant L. The results showed that no significant differences in hatchability were observed across all groups (p > 0.05). In ovo injection of recombinant L. lactis- HA1 markedly increased average daily gain (ADG), improved feed conversion ratio (FCR) (p < 0.05), and elevated indices for the thymus, spleen and bursa of Fabricius, and elevated serum HI titers, HA-specific IgG, IL-2, IL-4, and IFN-γ, as well as increased mucosal SIgA concentrations and strengthened HA1-specific lymphocyte proliferative responses (p < 0.05). Furthermore, this treatment increased VH and the VH/CD in both the duodenum and jejunum, and upregulated the transcriptional levels of intestinal barrier-associated genes (p < 0.05). Following H9N2 viral challenge, chicks in the recombinant L. lactis -HA1 group exhibited milder clinical manifestations and less body weight loss, along with numerically lower viral shedding titers and less pronounced pulmonary lesions compared with the PBS and L1 groups. Notably, it conferred protective effects that trended toward a level similar to that of the inactivated vaccine. Collectively, in ovo administration of recombinant L. lactis expressing HA1 accelerates early intestinal maturation, potentially in part through the intrinsic probiotic properties of L. lactis, and additionally induces HA1‐specific adaptive immune responses in broiler chicks. These findings provide a theoretical basis for developing novel in‐ovo lactic‐acid‐bacterium‐vectored vaccines against H9N2 avian influenza virus.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估使用表达 H9N2 禽流感 病毒血凝素 (HA) 亚基 1 (HA1) 蛋白的重组乳酸乳球菌作为一种新型卵内 疫苗 蛋白来保护雏鸡免受 H9N2 感染的潜力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及 160 个存活的含胚卵,随机分配到四组,这些卵接种了 PBS、灭活的 H9N2 疫苗、空乳酸乳球菌 媒介 或表达 HA1 的重组乳酸乳球菌。通过in ovo 疫苗接种进行评价。
elements_zh.methods: 通过评估 H9N2 病毒攻击后雏鸡的临床表现、体重减轻、病毒脱落滴度和肺部病变,评估重组乳酸乳球菌-HA1 的功效。此外,还测量了血清HI滴度、HA特异性IgG、IL-2、IL-4、IFN-γ、粘膜SIgA浓度和淋巴细胞增殖反应等免疫相关指标。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,卵内注射重组乳酸乳球菌-HA1可显着提高平均日增重(ADG)、饲料转化率(FCR)以及胸腺、脾脏、法氏囊等免疫指标,血清HI滴度,HA特异性IgG、IL-2、IL-4、IFN-γ以及粘膜SIgA浓度。它还增加了十二指肠和空肠中的 VH 和 VH/CD,并上调了肠屏障相关基因的转录。与 PBS 组和 L1 组相比,重组乳酸乳球菌-HA1 组的雏鸡临床症状较轻,体重减轻较少,病毒脱落滴度较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在蛋内施用表达 HA1 的重组乳酸乳球菌可加速早期肠道成熟,并在肉鸡中诱导 HA1 特异性适应性 免疫应答,这可能提供与灭活的 疫苗 类似的保护作用。

Notably, it conferred protective effects that trended toward a level similar to that of the inactivated vaccine. Collectively, in ovo administration of recombinant L. lactis expressing HA1 accelerates early intestinal maturation, potentially in part through the intrinsic probiotic properties of L. lactis, and additionally induces HA1‐specific adaptive immune responses in broiler chicks. These findings provide a theoretical basis for developing novel in‐ovo lactic‐acid‐bacterium‐vectored vaccines against H9N2 avian influenza virus.

title: Publicly Available Genomic Evidence for Nipah and Avian Influenza Viruses in Bangladesh: A Scoping Assessment of Metadata Completeness and Surveillance Representativeness at the Human–Animal Interface
abstract: Bangladesh experiences recurrent Nipah virus (NiV) outbreaks and sustained avian influenza virus (AIV) activity. Whether public genomic records contain metadata needed to assess surveillance representativeness across hosts, locations, and time is unclear.We conducted a structured, source-based scoping assessment of publicly documented NiV and AIV genomic records from Bangladesh (2001–2025), drawing on NCBI GenBank/INSDC and cited peer-reviewed and public-health sources. A pilot registry contained 108 entries (55 NiV, 53 AIV). Metadata were retained only when explicitly reported; unverified fields were recorded as not extracted. The registry is not a complete census. Five analytical questions were prespecified; several could not be evaluated because accession-level metadata were unavailable. The 33-accession AIV set containing H5N1 and H3N8 was excluded from H5/H9-specific interpretation. In the pilot registry, 9/108 entries (8.3%) had explicitly reported host species; the separate host-implied category was not added. Twelve entries (11.1%) had a full collection date; 21 (19.4%) had any collection date. Eight entries (7.4%) had an explicit district. The registry lists 22 NiV accession identifiers from a 2026 study, whereas the publication reports 23 newly sequenced N-gene records; this remains unresolved. Eight AIV accessions ( PV961349.1 – PV961356.1) represent eight segments of one chicken H5N1 isolate, not eight genomes. Twelve MN994-series records are HA-gene sequences from environmental live-bird-market samples.The pilot registry demonstrates substantial metadata limitations. Explicit host information was available for 8.3% of entries and explicit district for 7.4%; these prevent reliable quantitative assessment of host, district-level, and temporal representativeness and do not establish absence of surveillance or viral circulation. Accession-level reconstruction with transparent verification tiers and harmonised identifiers is required before quantitative representativeness indices or district-level priorities can be calculated.

title: Lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated DNA vaccine induces robust and durable immunity against avian influenza viruses in chickens
abstract: To evaluate the immunogenicity of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated DNA vaccines against avian influenza virus in chickens, hemagglutinin (HA) genes from three surrogate low pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV) subtypes, H2N2, H5N3, and H6N8, were cloned into an expression plasmid and formulated as monovalent or bivalent LNP-pDNA vaccines. A single intramuscular dose of 5 or 15 μg of monovalent LNP-pDNA vaccines induced strong hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody responses in chickens, with titers exceeding 1:64 and 1:128 respectively, whereas equivalent doses of naked DNA failed to elicit detectable HI antibodies. The bivalent LNP-pDNA vaccine containing H2 and H6 HA genes elicited HI antibody responses against both subtypes. Furthermore, a single immunization with the LNP-pDNA vaccine encoding the H5 antigen induced durable antibody responses, with HI titers above 1:32 maintained for nearly six months. At the 15-μg dose, the LNP-pDNA vaccine significantly reduced viral shedding in respiratory secretions and prevented detectable viral infection in the lungs following challenge with the homologous LPAIV H5N3 virus. Overall, LNP encapsulation markedly enhances the immunogenicity of pDNA vaccines in poultry. Thus, this study provides a proof-of-evidence that LNP-pDNA can be a safe and effective strategy for controlling avian influenza viruses in poultry.

title_zh: 脂质纳米粒子封装的 DNA 疫苗 在鸡中诱导针对 禽流感 病毒的强大而持久的免疫力
source_body_en: To evaluate the immunogenicity of lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated DNA vaccines against avian influenza virus in chickens, hemagglutinin (HA) genes from three surrogate low pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV) subtypes, H2N2, H5N3, and H6N8, were cloned into an expression plasmid and formulated as monovalent or bivalent LNP-pDNA vaccines. A single intramuscular dose of 5 or 15 μg of monovalent LNP-pDNA vaccines induced strong hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody responses in chickens, with titers exceeding 1:64 and 1:128 respectively, whereas equivalent doses of naked DNA failed to elicit detectable HI antibodies. The bivalent LNP-pDNA vaccine containing H2 and H6 HA genes elicited HI antibody responses against both subtypes. Furthermore, a single immunization with the LNP-pDNA vaccine encoding the H5 antigen induced durable antibody responses, with HI titers above 1:32 maintained for nearly six months. At the 15-μg dose, the LNP-pDNA vaccine significantly reduced viral shedding in respiratory secretions and prevented detectable viral infection in the lungs following challenge with the homologous LPAIV H5N3 virus. Overall, LNP encapsulation markedly enhances the immunogenicity of pDNA vaccines in poultry. Thus, this study provides a proof-of-evidence that LNP-pDNA can be a safe and effective strategy for controlling avian influenza viruses in poultry.

title: Protective Efficacy of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Vaccines Against Mortality in Chickens: A Meta-Analysis and Systematic Review of Experimental Challenge Trials
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) remains a major threat to poultry production and animal welfare. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between HPAI vaccination and mortality in experimentally challenged chickens and explored biological and operational sources of heterogeneity. Experimental studies comparing mortality in vaccinated and unvaccinated chickens following HPAI challenge were eligible. A Scopus search up to 30 of August 2025, supplemented by reference screening identified 66 eligible articles comprising 158 studies. Mortality relative risks (RRs) were analysed using random-effects models, with moderator analyses and exploratory multivariable sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool. Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (pooled RR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.08–0.14), although heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 88.4%). A trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis yielded a less pronounced protective association (RR = 0.335, 95% CI: 0.293–0.383). Univariate analyses suggested differences between vaccine platforms and administration routes, but exploratory adjusted comparisons were sensitive to model specification and incomplete characterisation of host immunity, antigen dose, adjuvant formulation, viral clade and challenge conditions. Inconsistent reporting of vaccine–challenge genetic and antigenic relationships prevented their reliable inclusion as moderators, while substantial unexplained heterogeneity remained. Risk-of-bias assessments revealed substantial methodological uncertainty, while inconsistent reporting of antigenic relationships prevented their reliable evaluation as moderators. Both recombinant and inactivated vaccines demonstrated protective associations against mortality, but the available evidence did not establish the intrinsic superiority of either platform. These findings support HPAI vaccination as a means of reducing mortality under experimental challenge while highlighting the need for better-characterised studies to evaluate antigenic matching, cross-protection and performance under field conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the protective efficacy of HPAI vaccines against mortality in chickens under experimental challenge. The review identified 158 studies from 66 eligible articles, with random-effects models used to analyze mortality relative risks. Vaccination was found to significantly reduce mortality (pooled RR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.08–0.14), although substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 88.4%) was observed. Both recombinant and inactivated vaccines showed protective effects, but no evidence of superiority between platforms was found. title_zh: 高致病性禽流感 疫苗 对鸡 死亡率 的保护功效:实验挑战试验的荟萃分析和系统评价
source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) remains a major threat to poultry production and animal welfare. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between HPAI vaccination and mortality in experimentally challenged chickens and explored biological and operational sources of heterogeneity. Experimental studies comparing mortality in vaccinated and unvaccinated chickens following HPAI challenge were eligible. A Scopus search up to 30 of August 2025, supplemented by reference screening identified 66 eligible articles comprising 158 studies. Mortality relative risks (RRs) were analysed using random-effects models, with moderator analyses and exploratory multivariable sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using the SYRCLE tool. Vaccination markedly reduced mortality (pooled RR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.08–0.14), although heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 88.4%). A trim-and-fill sensitivity analysis yielded a less pronounced protective association (RR = 0.335, 95% CI: 0.293–0.383). Univariate analyses suggested differences between vaccine platforms and administration routes, but exploratory adjusted comparisons were sensitive to model specification and incomplete characterisation of host immunity, antigen dose, adjuvant formulation, viral clade and challenge conditions. Inconsistent reporting of vaccine–challenge genetic and antigenic relationships prevented their reliable inclusion as moderators, while substantial unexplained heterogeneity remained. Risk-of-bias assessments revealed substantial methodological uncertainty, while inconsistent reporting of antigenic relationships prevented their reliable evaluation as moderators. Both recombinant and inactivated vaccines demonstrated protective associations against mortality, but the available evidence did not establish the intrinsic superiority of either platform. These findings support HPAI vaccination as a means of reducing mortality under experimental challenge while highlighting the need for better-characterised studies to evaluate antigenic matching, cross-protection and performance under field conditions.

title: Mortality in Wild Otters Linked to HPAI (H5N1) in Chile, 2023
abstract: This study documents molecular detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b in wild marine otters (Lontra felina) and a Southern river otter (Lontra provocax) in Chile in 2023. Analysis of official SERNAPESCA stranding records identified an increase in reported otter mortality in 2023 relative to previous years, coinciding geographically and temporally with the regional H5N1 outbreak in wild birds and mammals. Five individual otters yielded H5N1-positive RT-qPCR results across six specimens. Phylogenetic analyses of recovered viral sequences were consistent with the genetic diversity of viruses circulating in Chile and Peru during the South American outbreak. These molecular findings and epidemiological observations support an association between H5N1 circulation and reported otter mortality, but do not establish the cause of death of individual animals or the proportion of deaths attributable to infection. Integrated wildlife surveillance is warranted to better understand the potential impact of H5N1 on these vulnerable species.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 野生鸟类 中的 2023 H5N1 暴发 与哺乳动物之间的潜在联系以及智利野生水獭中 死亡率 的增加,以满足了解高致病性禽流感 (H5N1) 对海洋和河獭种群的生态和公共卫生影响的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了智利官方 SERNAPESCA 搁浅记录,以确定 2023 年水獭 死亡率 的增加,这在地理和时间上与 野生鸟类 和哺乳动物中的区域性 H5N1 暴发 一致。在六个样本中对五只水獭进行了测试。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 RT-qPCR 对五只水獭的标本进行 H5N1 分子检测,并对恢复的病毒序列进行系统发育分析,以评估其与南美 暴发 期间在智利和秘鲁传播的病毒的遗传关系。
elements_zh.main_results: 对搁浅记录的分析显示,与前几年相比,2023 年报告的水獭 死亡率 有所增加,与区域性 H5N1 暴发 一致。5 只水獭的 6 份样本的 RT-qPCR 结果呈 H5N1 阳性。病毒序列的系统发育分析与 暴发 期间在智利和秘鲁传播的病毒的遗传多样性一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,H5N1 病毒的传播与水獭 死亡率 之间可能存在关联,但并未证实死亡原因或因感染导致的死亡比例,这凸显了进一步开展针对性研究的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了综合野生动物 监测 的重要性,以更好地了解 H5N1 对脆弱水獭物种的影响,并为监测人畜共患流感 传播 的公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于有限数量样本的观察数据和分子测试,这可能无法完全确定因果关系或量化 H5N1 对水獭 死亡率 的贡献。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

title: pH-based inactivation of highly pathogenic H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk
abstract: ABSTRACT An outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 was confirmed in dairy cattle in March 2024 and subsequently spread to dairy herds throughout the United States, resulting in spillover cases in humans and other animals. Milk produced by infected dairy cattle, which has been shown to harbor high viral titers, poses a potential threat to peridomestic wildlife around dairies due to lack of treatment and disposal in wastewater systems that are often open to the environment. Here, we investigated a method for inactivating H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk, utilizing the irreversible conformational change of the hemagglutinin (HA) glycoprotein induced by low pH. The pH needed for complete inactivation of three distinct influenza A viruses was determined for subsequent use in acidifying milk. The use of common, readily available acidification solutions like vinegar demonstrated that a 3% final concentration of vinegar (pH 3.6) induced complete inactivation of H5N1 in unpasteurized milk after 60 min. Our results suggest that pH-based inactivation of H5N1 in unpasteurized milk is a quick, feasible strategy that could be used on dairy farms prior to disposal of contaminated milk, thus reducing the risks of environmental contamination and exposure of animals around farms. IMPORTANCE Dairy farms experiencing outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 generate large volumes of milk with high titers of infectious H5N1 virus. While milk from sick cows does not enter the consumer supply chain, disposal of this untreated, contaminated milk through on-site wastewater systems still poses a significant risk for environmental contamination and exposure of peridomestic wildlife, potentially leading to spillover events. A simple method for inactivation of virus in milk prior to disposal could mitigate this risk. We show that lowering the pH of virus-laden milk with commercially available vinegar can neutralize dairy cattle H5N1 virus within 1 h, providing a quick and effective strategy for potential use on dairies to inactivate the virus in milk before disposal.

analysis.research_question_and_background: An outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 in dairy cattle in March 2024 raised concerns about the potential threat of viral contamination in milk to peridomestic wildlife and humans. The study aimed to address the need for an effective method to inactivate H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study investigated the inactivation of H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk using pH manipulation. It focused on dairy farms in the United States where H5N1 outbreaks had occurred, and the research was conducted in a laboratory setting.
analysis.methods: The researchers determined the pH required for complete inactivation of three distinct influenza A viruses, including H5N1, and tested the effectiveness of acidification solutions like vinegar. They measured viral inactivation by assessing the loss of infectivity under controlled pH conditions.
analysis.main_results: A 3% final concentration of vinegar (pH 3.6) induced complete inactivation of H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk after 60 minutes. This method was effective in neutralizing the virus within one hour.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that pH-based inactivation using vinegar is a quick and feasible strategy for deactivating H5N1 virus in milk before disposal, offering a practical solution for reducing environmental contamination risks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method could inform strategies for dairy farms to safely manage contaminated milk, thereby reducing the risk of H5N1 virus transmission to peridomestic wildlife and humans.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a controlled laboratory environment, which may limit its applicability to real-world farm settings. However, the results are supported by direct experimental evidence and suggest a high level of confidence in the method's effectiveness.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the inactivation of H5N1 virus in unpasteurized milk using pH manipulation. An outbreak of H5N1 in dairy cattle in March 2024 highlighted the risk of viral contamination in milk to peridomestic wildlife and humans. The researchers tested acidification solutions like vinegar and found that a 3% concentration of vinegar (pH 3.6) completely inactivated the virus within 60 minutes. This method offers a quick and feasible strategy for dairy farms to reduce environmental contamination risks before disposing of contaminated milk. The study's results are based on direct experimental evidence, suggesting a high level of confidence in the approach. However, the controlled laboratory setting may limit real-world applicability. The findings could inform practices for managing contaminated milk on farms, thereby mitigating the spread of H5N1 virus to wildlife and humans.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2024 年 3 月,奶牛中检测到 高致病性禽流感 H5N1 的 暴发 引起了人们对牛奶中病毒污染对家境野生动物和人类的潜在威胁的担忧。该研究旨在解决对未经巴氏消毒牛奶中 H5N1 病毒灭活的有效方法的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究调查了使用 pH 值控制对未经巴氏消毒的牛奶中 H5N1 病毒的灭活情况。它主要针对发生 H5N1 暴发 的美国奶牛场,并且研究是在实验室环境中进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员确定了完全灭活三种不同甲型流感病毒(包括 H5N1)所需的 pH 值,并测试了醋等酸化溶液的有效性。他们通过评估受控 pH 条件下感染性的丧失来测量病毒灭活情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 60 分钟后,最终浓度为 3% 的醋(pH 3.6)可诱导未经巴氏消毒的牛奶中的 H5N1 病毒完全失活。这种方法在一小时内就能有效中和病毒。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,使用醋进行基于 pH 值的灭活是在牛奶处理前灭活牛奶中 H5N1 病毒的一种快速且可行的策略,为降低环境污染风险提供了实用的解决方案。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该方法可以为奶牛场提供安全管理受污染牛奶的策略,从而降低 H5N1 病毒 传播 对家境野生动物和人类的风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在受控实验室环境中进行的,这可能会限制其在现实农场环境中的适用性。然而,结果得到了直接实验证据的支持,并表明对该方法的有效性具有高度的信心。

analysis_zh.main_results: 60 分钟后,最终浓度为 3% 的醋(pH 3.6)可诱导未经巴氏消毒的牛奶中的 H5N1 病毒完全失活。这种方法在一小时内就能有效中和病毒。

title: Viral Pathogens as Global Health Threats: Review of Transmissibility, Lethality, and Pandemic Potential
abstract: Viral pathogens vary substantially in their transmissibility, lethality, and potential to cause widespread epidemics or pandemics. Measles, for example, is exceptionally contagious but has relatively low case fatality in populations with access to modern medical care. Conversely, rabies, Nipah virus, Ebola virus, and Marburg virus can cause severe disease with high case fatality rates but generally exhibit limited sustained human-to-human transmission. The greatest global threats, therefore, are not necessarily the most contagious or lethal viruses, but those that combine efficient transmission, substantial clinical severity, zoonotic reservoirs, evolutionary adaptability, and limited preventive or therapeutic options. The COVID-19 pandemic illustrated this convergence of risk factors, demonstrating how efficient transmission, including presymptomatic and asymptomatic spread, coupled with clinically significant disease can produce devastating global consequences. Influenza A viruses remain a major pandemic concern because of their extensive animal reservoirs, capacity for antigenic evolution, and established history of human pandemics. Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) is particularly concerning given the high case fatality observed among confirmed human cases, although sustained human-to-human transmission has not been established. In contrast, henipaviruses and filoviruses pose substantial clinical threats because of their high lethality, despite comparatively limited transmissibility. This review critically examines major viral threats through three interconnected determinants of global health risk: transmissibility, infection fatality risk, and the biological and epidemiological factors governing their epidemic and pandemic potential.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on avian influenza A viruses, examining their transmissibility, infection fatality risk, and pandemic potential. The central question is how these viruses pose global health threats through their biological and epidemiological characteristics.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a critical analysis of major viral threats, with an emphasis on avian influenza A viruses. It does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria, but it systematically evaluates the interplay of transmissibility, lethality, and pandemic potential across various viral entities.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Avian influenza A viruses, particularly highly pathogenic strains like H5N1, are significant global health threats due to their high case fatality rates, zoonotic reservoirs, and potential for evolutionary adaptability. However, sustained human-to-human transmission remains unestablished for these viruses, highlighting the need for further research.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is limited evidence on sustained human-to-human transmission of avian influenza A viruses, particularly for highly pathogenic subtypes like H5N1. Additionally, the review notes that while these viruses have high lethality, their transmissibility is generally limited, creating a gap in understanding their full pandemic potential.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to better understand the transmissibility and evolutionary adaptability of avian influenza A viruses, especially in the context of zoonotic spillover events. Surveillance and diagnostic improvements are also critical to monitor and respond to outbreaks effectively.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates avian influenza A viruses as significant global health threats, emphasizing their high case fatality rates and zoonotic potential. While these viruses are not highly contagious among humans, their ability to cause severe disease and adapt to new hosts raises concerns about pandemic potential. The review highlights the need for improved surveillance, diagnostics, and research to understand their transmissibility and evolutionary dynamics. Key findings include the role of H5N1 in human infections and the importance of monitoring avian-origin zoonotic infections. The review also notes gaps in evidence regarding sustained human-to-human transmission and the full extent of their pandemic risk.

title: Proximity Proteomics Reveals Interactome Rewiring Driven by the Mammalian-Adaptive PB2-E627K Mutation of Avian Influenza Polymerase
abstract: Abstract The polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) E627K substitution in the influenza A virus polymerase is a key determinant of mammalian adaptation, yet its impact on the host interaction remains incompletely understood. Using TurboID proximity labeling in human cells, we profiled host proteins associated with wild-type and E627K mutant H5N1 polymerase in both isolated PB2 and trimeric (PA-PB1-PB2) contexts, identifying 204 high-confidence proximal interactions. Polymerase assembly drives the PB2-associated interactome, with substantially expanded host interactions detected in the trimeric context compared to PB2 alone. E627K remodels host associations, shifting interactions related to cellular structural organization and intracellular trafficking while preserving nuclear transport and RNP assembly. WT-associated but E627K-lost proteins relate to host RNA processing and protein quality control pathways. Differential interaction scoring distinguished polymerase assembly dependent interactions from PB2-alone associations. Integration of coimmunoprecipitation and AlphaFold3 provided complementary evidence for representative interactions and revealed host factors engage polymerase through subunits other than PB2, highlighting the importance of the assembled complex for interaction recognition. Together, these findings demonstrate that PB2-E627K selectively redistributes interaction preferences within a conserved functional landscape. This study provides a resource for understanding influenza virus adaptation and identifies candidate host factors for further investigation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impact of the PB2-E627K mutation on host interactions of avian influenza A viruses, as this mutation is a key determinant of mammalian adaptation but its effects on host interaction remain incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used TurboID proximity labeling in human cells to profile host proteins associated with wild-type and E627K mutant H5N1 polymerase in both isolated PB2 and trimeric (PA-PB1-PB2) contexts, identifying 204 high-confidence proximal interactions.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed TurboID proximity labeling in human cells and integrated coimmunoprecipitation with AlphaFold3 to provide complementary evidence for representative interactions and reveal host factors engaging the polymerase through subunits other than PB2.
analysis.main_results: Polymerase assembly drives the PB2-associated interactome, with substantially expanded host interactions detected in the trimeric context compared to PB2 alone. E627K remodels host associations, shifting interactions related to cellular structural organization and intracellular trafficking while preserving nuclear transport and RNP assembly.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the PB2-E627K mutation selectively redistributes interaction preferences within a conserved functional landscape, highlighting the importance of the assembled complex for interaction recognition.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides a resource for understanding influenza virus adaptation and identifies candidate host factors for further investigation, which could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and therapeutic strategies for avian influenza.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on high-confidence proximal interactions identified through TurboID proximity labeling and AlphaFold3 integration, providing moderate confidence in the observed findings.

The study provides insights into influenza virus adaptation and highlights candidate host factors for further research. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract data, limiting the confidence in the conclusions to moderate.

title_zh: 邻近蛋白质组学揭示了由 禽流感 聚合酶的哺乳动物适应性 PB2-E627K 突变 驱动的相互作用组重新布线
source_body_en: Abstract The polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) E627K substitution in the influenza A virus polymerase is a key determinant of mammalian adaptation, yet its impact on the host interaction remains incompletely understood. Using TurboID proximity labeling in human cells, we profiled host proteins associated with wild-type and E627K mutant H5N1 polymerase in both isolated PB2 and trimeric (PA-PB1-PB2) contexts, identifying 204 high-confidence proximal interactions. Polymerase assembly drives the PB2-associated interactome, with substantially expanded host interactions detected in the trimeric context compared to PB2 alone. E627K remodels host associations, shifting interactions related to cellular structural organization and intracellular trafficking while preserving nuclear transport and RNP assembly. WT-associated but E627K-lost proteins relate to host RNA processing and protein quality control pathways. Differential interaction scoring distinguished polymerase assembly dependent interactions from PB2-alone associations. Integration of coimmunoprecipitation and AlphaFold3 provided complementary evidence for representative interactions and revealed host factors engage polymerase through subunits other than PB2, highlighting the importance of the assembled complex for interaction recognition. Together, these findings demonstrate that PB2-E627K selectively redistributes interaction preferences within a conserved functional landscape. This study provides a resource for understanding influenza virus adaptation and identifies candidate host factors for further investigation.

title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30 runs each, yielding 5,400 responses. Pairwise cosine similarity was computed on MPNet embeddings, with sensitivity analyses across three additional transformers. Statistical inference combined standard nonparametric tests (paired Wilcoxon and Friedman with Holm--Bonferroni correction) with inter-embedding agreement statistics (ICC(2,k) and Cronbach's $\alpha$) introduced here as a methodological addition. Both models produced high mean consistency (0.93--0.97, rescaled to {[}0, 1{]}). GPT-5 showed reproducibility significantly higher than repeatability (W = 3.0, p = 0.0003), whereas for Gemini 3 Flash the two metrics were statistically indistinguishable (W = 42.0, p = 0.33). Differential Diagnosis ranked among the top two CoT framings for consistency in both models. The tested chatbots behave as semantically stable sources on H5N1 One Health questions, and the developed consistency evaluation framework is portable to other domains.

title_zh: GPT-5 和 Gemini 3 Flash 对 H5N1 One Health 问题的语义重复性和再现性
source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30 runs each, yielding 5,400 responses. Pairwise cosine similarity was computed on MPNet embeddings, with sensitivity analyses across three additional transformers. Statistical inference combined standard nonparametric tests (paired Wilcoxon and Friedman with Holm--Bonferroni correction) with inter-embedding agreement statistics (ICC(2,k) and Cronbach's $\alpha$) introduced here as a methodological addition. Both models produced high mean consistency (0.93--0.97, rescaled to {[}0, 1{]}). GPT-5 showed reproducibility significantly higher than repeatability (W = 3.0, p = 0.0003), whereas for Gemini 3 Flash the two metrics were statistically indistinguishable (W = 42.0, p = 0.33). Differential Diagnosis ranked among the top two CoT framings for consistency in both models. The tested chatbots behave as semantically stable sources on H5N1 One Health questions, and the developed consistency evaluation framework is portable to other domains.

title: Development of a sensitive and rapid on-site detection method for avian influenza virus in wildlife using reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification.
abstract: The global spread of H5 high pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) severely threatens wildlife, posing a critical challenge for conservation medicine. Although immunochromatographic (IC) kits are commonly used for on-site diagnosis of wildlife samples, their low sensitivity often results in false negatives. Highly sensitive molecular methods, such as reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), are often impractical for field use because of the need for sophisticated equipment. Therefore, a sensitive and affordable on-site diagnostic tool is essential for early detection of HPAIV in wildlife samples collected in the field. In this study, a reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assay targeting M gene for the on-site detection of avian influenza virus (AIV) was developed and evaluated. Initially, the assay using liquid reagents was validated in terms of specificity and sensitivity to confirm the appropriateness of the reaction mixture composition. This assay exhibited high specificity and exclusively detected AIVs without cross-reactivity. Sensitivity analysis using swabs from HPAIV-infected ducks demonstrated that the assay was comparable to RT-qPCR but substantially superior to IC kits. The reaction reagents were lyophilized to minimize the testing procedure for practical field use. This simplified protocol using lyophilized reagents and a portable incubator yielded results that were highly concordant with those of RT-qPCR. These findings indicate that the RT-LAMP assay serves as a robust diagnostic resource, supporting wildlife conservation strategies by enabling rapid, sensitive, and early detection of AIV infection in the field.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science

The assay was simplified using lyophilized reagents and a portable incubator, making it suitable for field use. The findings suggest that the RT-LAMP assay is a robust diagnostic tool for early detection of AIV in wildlife, which can support conservation strategies. However, the study was limited to testing on HPAIV-infected ducks, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate.

abstract_zh: H5高致病性禽流感病毒(HPAIV)的全球传播严重威胁野生动物,对保护医学提出严峻挑战。尽管免疫色谱 (IC) 试剂盒通常用于野生动物样本的现场 诊断,但其低灵敏度常常会导致假阴性。高度灵敏的分子方法,例如逆转录定量聚合酶链式反应 (RT-qPCR),由于需要复杂的设备,通常在现场使用时不切实际。因此,灵敏且经济实惠的现场诊断工具对于在野外采集的野生动物样本中早期检测 HPAIV 至关重要。在本研究中,开发并评估了一种针对 M 基因的逆转录环介导等温扩增 (RT-LAMP) 检测方法,用于现场检测 禽流感 病毒 (AIV)。最初,使用液体试剂进行的测定在特异性和灵敏度方面进行了验证,以确认反应混合物组成的适当性。该测定表现出高特异性,并且专门检测 AIV,且无交叉反应。使用 HPAIV 感染鸭的拭子进行的敏感性分析表明,该检测方法与 RT-qPCR 相当,但明显优于 IC 试剂盒。反应试剂被冻干,以最大限度地减少实际现场使用的测试程序。这种使用冻干试剂和便携式培养箱的简化方案产生的结果与 RT-qPCR 的结果高度一致。这些发现表明,RT-LAMP 检测可作为一种强大的诊断资源,通过在现场快速、灵敏和早期检测 AIV 感染来支持野生动物保护策略。

title: Structural and functional characterization of hemagglutinin E190D and Q226H minor variants in human H5N1 A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024
abstract: In late 2024, an avian H5N1 influenza virus derived from clade 2.3.4.4b was isolated from a severe human infection in British Columbia (A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024), revealing a rare combination of substitutions E190D and Q226H as minor variants in the receptor-binding site (RBS). We recombinantly produced hemagglutinins (HA) harboring these mutations and conducted receptor-binding and structural analyses. The wild-type HA with hallmark residues E190 and Q226 retained strong binding to α2-3 N-linked glycans, whereas E190D and Q226H abolished binding to α2-3 N- and O-linked glycans and no switch to α2-6 sialosides. The bulkier H226 caused steric clashes within the RBS, whereas E190D eliminated a conserved hydrogen bond with Sia-1, disrupting receptor engagement. Although D190 and H226 in this isolate are deleterious to engagement with known glycan receptors and not compatible with human-to-human transmission, continued surveillance is essential to monitor any changes in key RBS residues in circulating H5N1 viruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the impact of minor variants E190D and Q226H in the receptor-binding site (RBS) of an avian H5N1 influenza virus isolated from a severe human infection in British Columbia, as these substitutions were identified as rare and potentially significant for viral function.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved recombinant production of hemagglutinins (HA) with the E190D and Q226H mutations and conducted receptor-binding and structural analyses on these variants, comparing them to the wild-type HA with hallmark residues E190 and Q226.
analysis.methods: The researchers produced recombinant hemagglutinins (HA) with the E190D and Q226H mutations and performed receptor-binding assays and structural analyses to evaluate their interactions with glycan receptors.
analysis.main_results: The wild-type HA retained strong binding to α2-3 N-linked glycans, while the E190D and Q226H variants abolished binding to both α2-3 N- and O-linked glycans and did not switch to α2-6 sialosides. The Q226H mutation caused steric clashes within the RBS, and the E190D mutation eliminated a conserved hydrogen bond with Sia-1, disrupting receptor engagement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that the E190D and Q226H substitutions in the RBS of this H5N1 isolate are detrimental to receptor binding, which may hinder its ability to engage with human receptors, though continued surveillance is necessary to monitor potential changes in circulating viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results highlight the importance of monitoring key receptor-binding site (RBS) residues in H5N1 viruses to assess their potential for adaptation and transmission to humans, informing surveillance and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to structural and functional analyses of recombinant hemagglutinins, and the evidence is based on in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent in vivo behavior. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of minor variants E190D and Q226H in the receptor-binding site (RBS) of an avian H5N1 influenza virus isolated from a severe human infection in British Columbia. The researchers produced recombinant hemagglutinins (HA) with these mutations and conducted receptor-binding and structural analyses. The wild-type HA retained strong binding to α2-3 N-linked glycans, whereas the E190D and Q226H variants abolished binding to both α2-3 N- and O-linked glycans and did not switch to α2-6 sialosides. The Q226H mutation caused steric clashes within the RBS, and the E190D mutation disrupted a conserved hydrogen bond with Sia-1, impairing receptor engagement. The authors suggest that these substitutions may hinder the virus's ability to engage with human receptors, though continued surveillance is essential to monitor potential changes in circulating H5N1 viruses. The study's findings have implications for understanding the functional impact of these variants and their relevance to public health, but the evidence is based on in vitro experiments, limiting its generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查从不列颠哥伦比亚省严重人类感染中分离出的禽 H5N1 流感病毒的受体结合位点 (RBS) 中的微小变异 E190D 和 Q226H 的影响,因为这些替换被认为是罕见的,并且对病毒功能可能具有重要意义。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及使用 E190D 和 Q226H 突变 重组生产血凝素 (HA),并对这些变体进行受体结合和结构分析,将它们与具有标志残基 E190 和 Q226 的野生型 HA 进行比较。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员用 E190D 和 Q226H 突变 生产了重组血凝素 (HA),并进行了受体结合测定和结构分析,以评估它们与聚糖受体的相互作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 野生型 HA 保留了与 α2-3 N 连接聚糖的强结合,而 E190D 和 Q226H 变体消除了与 α2-3 N 连接聚糖和 O 连接聚糖的结合,并且没有转换为 α2-6 唾液酸苷。Q226H 突变 引起 RBS 内的空间冲突,E190D 突变 消除了与 Sia-1 的保守氢键,破坏了受体的结合。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,该 H5N1 分离株的 RBS 中的 E190D 和 Q226H 取代不利于受体结合,这可能会阻碍其与人类受体结合的能力,尽管持续的 监测 对于监测循环病毒的潜在变化是必要的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果凸显了监测 H5N1 病毒中关键受体结合位点 (RBS) 残基以评估其对人类的适应潜力和 传播 的重要性,为 监测 和公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于重组血凝素的结构和功能分析,证据基于体外实验,可能无法完全代表体内行为。证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 2024 年末,从不列颠哥伦比亚省的严重人类感染中分离出源自进化枝 2.3.4.4b 的禽 H5N1 流感病毒 (A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024),揭示了 E190D 和 Q226H 替换的罕见组合,作为受体结合位点 (RBS) 中的微小变异。我们重组产生了含有这些 突变 的血凝素 (HA),并进行了受体结合和结构分析。具有标志残基 E190 和 Q226 的野生型 HA 保留了与 α2-3 N 连接聚糖的强结合,而 E190D 和 Q226H 消除了与 α2-3 N 连接聚糖和 O 连接聚糖的结合,并且没有转换为 α2-6 唾液酸苷。体积较大的 H226 引起 RBS 内的空间冲突,而 E190D 消除了与 Sia-1 的保守氢键,破坏了受体的结合。尽管该分离株中的 D190 和 H226 不利于与已知聚糖受体的结合,并且与人与人之间的 传播 不相容,但持续的 传播 对于监测循环 H5N1 病毒中关键 RBS 残基的任何变化至关重要。

title: Integrating Epidemiology and Host Immunogenomics Against Transboundary Animal Viral Threats
abstract: Transboundary animal viruses cross national borders and, increasingly, species barriers. Since 2019, lumpy skin disease virus has spread across Asia and into Western Europe, peste des petits ruminants virus has entered the European Union, foot-and-mouth disease has reemerged in Central Europe, and H5N1 avian influenza has become established in dairy cattle. These threats are usually studied from two separate perspectives. Field and genomic epidemiology describe where viruses circulate, how they spread, and what they cost, whereas host immunogenomics investigates why some animals resist infection or respond better to vaccination. Integrating these perspectives can provide a more complete understanding of host–pathogen interactions and inform more effective disease prevention and control. This review examines six representative viruses: peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV), foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV), African swine fever virus (ASFV), lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV), porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV), and H5N1 avian influenza virus, and the threats they pose to animal health and production. We summarize the epidemiological and immunogenomic approaches available to investigate these threats and propose an integrated framework linking both fields to four control outcomes: targeted surveillance, improved vaccine matching, selective breeding for disease resistance, and evidence-informed policymaking. We also assess the feasibility of this framework in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and smallholder farming systems, where disease burdens are high but the evidence base remains limited, and we highlight that host genomic research is concentrated in pigs despite the heavy disease burden in small ruminants. By connecting population-level patterns of viral transmission with host-level variation in susceptibility and immune response, this review identifies opportunities to strengthen the surveillance and control of transboundary animal viral diseases.

title_original: Integrating Epidemiology and Host Immunogenomics Against Transboundary Animal Viral Threats

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on avian influenza A viruses, examining their role in transboundary animal viral threats, particularly their impact on animal health and production. It explores how these viruses cross national and species borders and investigates the integration of epidemiology and host immunogenomics to better understand host–pathogen interactions and improve disease prevention and control.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of six representative viruses, including avian influenza A viruses. It outlines the epidemiological and immunogenomic approaches used to study these viruses and proposes an integrated framework for disease control. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but emphasizes the synthesis of available evidence.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that avian influenza A viruses pose significant transboundary threats, particularly in regions where they have become established in dairy cattle and other livestock. It concludes that integrating epidemiological and immunogenomic data can enhance understanding of host–pathogen dynamics and lead to more effective disease control strategies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that host genomic research is disproportionately focused on pigs, despite the high disease burden in small ruminants. It also identifies gaps in the evidence base for low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and smallholder farming systems, where disease control is most challenging.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes specific research and practice priorities, including targeted surveillance, improved vaccine matching, selective breeding for disease resistance, and evidence-informed policymaking. It emphasizes the need for more genomic research on small ruminants and better integration of data across different host species and regions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the transboundary threats posed by avian influenza A viruses, emphasizing their spread across species and regions. It highlights the need to integrate epidemiological and immunogenomic approaches to better understand host–pathogen interactions and improve disease prevention and control. The review identifies gaps in genomic research for small ruminants and challenges in low- and middle-income countries. It proposes actionable strategies such as targeted surveillance, improved vaccine development, and evidence-based policies to address these threats. The integration of these perspectives is seen as critical for strengthening disease control efforts.

abstract_zh: 跨境动物病毒跨越国界,并越来越多地跨越物种障碍。2019年以来,块状皮肤病病毒在亚洲蔓延并进入西欧,小反刍兽疫病毒进入欧盟,口蹄疫在中欧重新出现,H5N1 禽流感在奶牛中扎根。通常从两个不同的角度研究这些威胁。现场和基因组 流行病学 描述了病毒在哪里传播、如何传播以及它们的成本,而 宿主 免疫基因组学则研究为什么一些动物能够抵抗感染或对 疫苗接种 做出更好的反应。整合这些观点可以更全面地了解 宿主 与病原体的相互作用,并为更有效的疾病预防和控制提供信息。本综述研究了六种代表性病毒:小反刍兽疫病毒(PPRV)、口蹄疫病毒(FMDV)、非洲猪瘟病毒(ASFV)、结节性皮肤病病毒(LSDV)、猪繁殖与呼吸综合征病毒(PRRSV)和H5N1 禽流感病毒,以及它们对动物健康和生产构成的威胁。我们总结了可用于调查这些威胁的流行病学和免疫基因组学方法,并提出了一个将这两个领域与四种控制结果联系起来的综合框架:有针对性的 监测、改进的 疫苗 匹配、抗病选择性育种以及循证决策。我们还评估了该框架在低收入和中等收入国家(LMIC)和小农农业系统中的可行性,这些国家的疾病负担很高,但证据基础仍然有限,并且我们强调,尽管小反刍动物的疾病负担很重,但 宿主 基因组研究集中在猪身上。通过将病毒 传播 的群体水平模式与 宿主 水平的易感性变异和 免疫应答 连接起来,本综述确定了加强 监测 和跨境动物病毒性疾病控制的机会。

title: Balancing Animal Welfare and Avian Influenza Biosecurity in Small-Scale Free-Range Chicken Systems
abstract: Small-scale outdoor chicken keeping creates a difficult biosecurity problem. Outdoor access supports valued husbandry but can expose flocks to wildlife and contaminated environments. This structured narrative review synthesised 20 purposively selected sources, based on HPAI exposure and welfare-related control in small outdoor flocks. The selected evidence showed that routine husbandry and farm connections also shaped exposure. Direct animal-based welfare evidence was scarce; most welfare-relevant work examined keeper concerns or practical consequences. Cleaner daily management may be combined with targeted wildlife measures and vaccination, although their joint performance in small flocks remains uncertain. Because uptake depends on local conditions and practical burden, awareness does not ensure sustained practice. Biosecurity should therefore address a credible exposure pathway without creating avoidable harm or an impractical burden. Future studies should use standardised welfare indicators and longitudinal field data to evaluate whether combined interventions can reduce HPAI exposure while maintaining acceptable welfare standards. This evidence would support the development of proportionate, practical, and locally adaptable biosecurity guidance for small-scale outdoor chicken keepers.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the biosecurity challenges in small-scale free-range chicken systems related to avian influenza A viruses. The central question is how to balance animal welfare with effective biosecurity measures to prevent exposure to avian influenza A viruses and other related pathogens.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a structured narrative synthesis of 20 purposively selected sources, with a focus on HPAI exposure and welfare-related control in small outdoor flocks. The evidence base includes studies on the impact of outdoor access on avian influenza A virus exposure and the role of routine husbandry and farm connections in shaping this exposure.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The evidence indicates that routine husbandry and farm connections significantly influence exposure to avian influenza A viruses. However, direct animal-based welfare evidence is limited, with most studies examining keeper concerns or practical consequences rather than direct welfare outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a lack of direct animal-based welfare evidence, and most studies focus on keeper concerns rather than the actual welfare of the chickens. Additionally, the joint performance of interventions such as cleaner daily management, targeted wildlife measures, and vaccination in reducing HPAI exposure while maintaining welfare standards remains uncertain.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should use standardised welfare indicators and longitudinal field data to evaluate the effectiveness of combined interventions in reducing HPAI exposure while maintaining acceptable welfare standards. This evidence would support the development of proportionate, practical, and locally adaptable biosecurity guidance for small-scale outdoor chicken keepers.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the biosecurity challenges in small-scale free-range chicken systems related to avian influenza A viruses. It highlights the role of outdoor access in exposing flocks to wildlife and contaminated environments, and how routine husbandry and farm connections further shape this exposure. The review notes that direct animal-based welfare evidence is scarce, with most studies focusing on keeper concerns or practical consequences. It suggests that cleaner daily management, targeted wildlife measures, and vaccination may be combined to address HPAI exposure, although their effectiveness in small flocks is uncertain. The review calls for future studies to use standardised welfare indicators and longitudinal data to assess the impact of combined interventions. It concludes that proportionate, practical, and locally adaptable biosecurity guidance is needed to balance animal welfare and HPAI prevention in these systems.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是对 20 个有意选择的来源的结构化叙述综合,重点是小型户外鸡群中高致病性禽流感的暴露和与福利相关的控制。证据基础包括关于户外活动对 禽流感 A 病毒暴露的影响以及常规畜牧业和农场联系在形成这种暴露中的作用的研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 证据表明,日常饲养和农场联系显着影响 禽流感 A 病毒的暴露。然而,直接基于动物的福利证据是有限的,大多数研究检查饲养员的担忧或实际后果,而不是直接的福利结果。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 缺乏直接的基于动物的福利证据,大多数研究关注饲养员的担忧,而不是鸡的实际福利。此外,清洁日常管理、有针对性的野生动物措施和 疫苗接种 等干预措施在减少高致病性禽流感暴露同时维持福利标准方面的联合表现仍不确定。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应使用标准化福利指标和纵向现场数据来评估综合干预措施在减少高致病性禽流感暴露同时维持可接受的福利标准方面的有效性。这一证据将支持为小规模户外养鸡者制定适当的、实用的、适合当地的生物安全指南。

abstract_zh: 小规模的户外养鸡造成了一个棘手的生物安全问题。户外通道支持有价值的畜牧业,但可能使羊群暴露于野生动物和受污染的环境中。这篇结构化的叙述性评论综合了 20 个有目的地选择的来源,基于小型户外鸡群的高致病性禽流感暴露和与福利相关的控制。选定的证据表明,日常饲养和农场联系也会影响暴露程度。直接基于动物的福利证据很少;大多数与福利相关的工作都考察了饲养员的担忧或实际后果。清洁的日常管理可以与有针对性的野生动物措施和 疫苗接种 相结合,尽管它们在小群中的联合表现仍不确定。因为吸收取决于当地条件和实际负担,意识并不能确保持续的实践。因此,生物安全应解决可靠的暴露途径,而不造成可避免的伤害或不切实际的负担。未来的研究应使用标准化福利指标和纵向现场数据来评估联合干预措施是否可以减少高致病性禽流感暴露,同时保持可接受的福利标准。这一证据将支持为小规模户外养鸡者制定适当的、实用的、适合当地的生物安全指南。
